handoff.purpose: Module-level docstring and imports for the killswitch module.

claims.text: A permit file, not a stop file. The loop runs only while a file on disk holds the exact token ``RUN`` on its first non-empty line.
claims.why: No code in this chunk implements reading a permit file; the claim refers to behavior of KillSwitch.read_state which is not defined here.

claims.text: A human in another terminal halts the loop with: ``python -m daedalus.spine.killswitch stop``
claims.why: No __main__ block or CLI handling is present in this chunk; the claim refers to external entry point.

claims.text: ``del`` on the permit works just as well, which matters at 3am.
claims.why: No code handling deletion of permit file is present; claim refers to behavior not in chunk.

claims.text: Presence-means-stop (the obvious design) was rejected because it fails OPEN on every interesting failure. ... Absence-means-stop inverts every one of those: any question this module cannot answer becomes STOP.
claims.why: The design rationale is described but not implemented in this chunk; no code to verify absence-means-stop logic.

claims.text: There is no code path in :meth:`KillSwitch.read_state` that returns "running" without having positively read the token.
claims.why: KillSwitch.read_state is not defined in this chunk; claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: OBSERVATION -- the switch latches within ONE poll interval of the permit changing on disk (default 0.25 s). MEASURED at a 0.1 s poll, across a *process boundary* ... 215 / 222 / 225 / 233 / 239 ms over five runs, against a 600 ms budget (``test_latency_latch_within_one_poll_interval``).
claims.why: No test function or measurement code present in this chunk; claim refers to external test.

claims.text: CHILD DEATH -- the whole process TREE is dead, and the gate has given up, within the same window. MEASURED on the real :func:`daedalus.spine.attempt.pytest_gate` path ... 257 / 258 / 262 / 268 / 425 ms (cold first run last), against a 3.0 s budget (``test_latency_gate_child_tree_dies``).
claims.why: No implementation of child death or test present; references external module and test.

claims.text: NO NEW SPEND -- no attempt and no provider call is *started* after the latch, because :meth:`checkpoint` raises. An HTTP request already in flight is NOT aborted.
claims.why: checkpoint method not defined in this chunk; claim about its behavior unverifiable.

claims.text: Once :meth:`should_stop` has answered True it answers True forever, in memory, for the life of the object.
claims.why: should_stop method not defined in this chunk; monotonic property unverifiable.

claims.text: The permit lives in ``%LOCALAPPDATA%/daedalus/control/<repo-digest>/``, a SIBLING of ``%LOCALAPPDATA%/daedalus/worktrees/`` ... inheritance flows DOWN a tree, never sideways -- so no amount of labelling in ``worktrees/`` can ever reach ``control/``.
claims.why: No path construction or containment logic present in this chunk; refers to external functions.

claims.text: A candidate under :func:`daedalus.spine.containment.spawn_contained` (Low integrity) is refused by the KERNEL when it tries to delete the permit, overwrite it with ``RUN``, delete the ``.stopped`` marker, or create either. Measured in ``test_contained_candidate_cannot_defeat_it``
claims.why: No containment logic or test present in this chunk; references external functions.

claims.text: A candidate NOT under containment, running at the operator's own integrity level, CAN rewrite both files. It still cannot un-latch a switch that has already read STOP (``test_uncontained_forgery_cannot_unlatch``).
claims.why: No implementation or test present; claim unverifiable.

claims.text: :meth:`KillSwitch.stop_children` calls :func:`daedalus.spine.cancel.cancel_all_managed`, which cancels EVERY live ``ManagedProcess`` in this interpreter -- not merely the ones handed to :meth:`KillSwitch.track`.
claims.why: stop_children and track methods not defined; cancel_all_managed from external module not present.

claims.text: The cost is that a kill switch in a process that hosts more than the loop (a web API, a REPL) will also kill that other work. For an unattended loop driver that is correct and is the point; for anything else, construct the switch with ``sweep_managed=False`` and rely on :meth:`track` plus the cancel token.
claims.why: No constructor or sweep_managed parameter visible; claim unverifiable.

claims.text: WHY THERE IS NO LOCK HERE ... writes go through ``os.replace`` (atomic on both platforms), so a reader sees the old bytes or the new bytes and never a torn file, and a read that fails for ANY reason -- including a Windows sharing violation -- is already STOP.
claims.why: No file read/write code present in this chunk; claim about atomicity and failure handling unverifiable.
